incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1: Inference-pool-3 node flapping (NotReady) x3 in past 5m. Affected pods: redwood-infer-runtime-* in pool inference-prod-3. Auto-escalation to oncall. https://alerts.redwood.internal/INC-1029

mohit (oncall): on it. paging details show kubelet restarts on node ip-10-2-45-11 and ip-10-2-45-12. seeing 503s to customers? anyone else? :eyes:

julia (eng-runtime): I'm seeing container restarts + OOMKilled in the runtime logs for a few pods. Looks correlated with node flaps. Dumping tails now.

sam (eng-sre): grabbing node metrics. NotReady spikes line up with kubelet crash loop from system logs. kernel messages show `dram unavailable` style OOM events? pulling dmesg.

mohit (oncall): kate, any customer-facing alerts already?

kate (support): support queue: ~20 active tickets referencing model timeouts and errors. prod-embed requests affected intermittently. We sent initial message to top affected customers. They want ETA.

julia (eng-runtime): tail from one runtime pod: ```
2026-02-26T14:21:03Z runtime ERROR: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 256MB for KV cache
2026-02-26T14:21:03Z runtime INFO: container restarting (OOMKilled)
2026-02-26T14:21:04Z kubelet WARNING: Eviction threshold crossed
```

sam (eng-sre): dmesg snippet from node ip-10-2-45-11: ```
[178420.123456] Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (containerd) score 987 or sacrifice child
[178420.123460] Killed process 4321 (containerd) total-vm:...
[178421.000000] systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed status=9
```

mohit (oncall): ok so nodes are OOMing -> kubelet restarts -> nodes go NotReady -> pods get evicted then crash on restart. This is causing the inference pool degradation.

julia (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a pattern: a set of large requests (long sequences) create big KV cache growth; combined with other processes pushing GPU/host memory we hit OOM. Probably a regression in request batching config.

sam (eng-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) cordon ip-10-2-45-11 and ip-10-2-45-12 2) scale up inference-prod-3 pool by 30% to get capacity spread 3) remove pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff 4) restart kubelet after we free memory. I'll run those now.

mohit (oncall): please also activate fallback routing to inference-prod-2 (region replica) so customer requests get routed away. Julia, can we disable large-sequence batching temporarily?

julia (eng-runtime): yes I can flip batching window down to 50ms and cap prefix length to 3k tokens for pool inference-prod-3 via runtime config. Pushing config change.

sam (eng-sre): cordoned nodes and started scale-up. K8s scale command: `kubectl scale --replicas=40 deployment/redwood-infer-runtime -n prod`

sam (eng-sre): also evicted the heaviest pods and forced node memory reclaim. monitoring shows CPU steady and node memory free increasing.

julia (eng-runtime): runtime config change applied: reduced batch window + prefix cap. Logs show fewer KV allocations now.

mohit (oncall): incident-bot: note mitigation actions in INC-1029 ticket. Kate, update customers: we are routing requests away and applying config mitigations; ETA 15-30m to stabilize.

kate (support): sent update to affected customers and posted public status: "Partial degraded performance for some generation requests; mitigation in progress". Will escalate any inbound P1s. :white_check_mark:

sam (eng-sre): two things to follow: we should check kubelet cgroup memory limits and also identify any recent runtime image changes. I see a recent config bump to `--kv-cache-size` on 02/24 in runtime repo. Tagging eng-runtime.

julia (eng-runtime): noted. I'll open PR to revert the kv-cache-size bump if we confirm it's the culprit. For now keep reduced batching.

mohit (oncall): monitoring: 503 rate down from 6% -> 1.2% after scaling + reroute. Node flaps stopped for ip-10-2-45-11, one restart for kubelet completed. ip-10-2-45-12 still showing kubelet restart loop but less frequent.

sam (eng-sre): executing `systemctl stop kubelet` and waiting 30s before `systemctl start kubelet` on the remaining unstable node after eviction to avoid immediate crash loop. Doing now.

julia (eng-runtime): runtime pods rescheduled onto healthy nodes, GPU memory use per-pod down ~20%. No new OOMs seen in last 6 minutes.

mohit (oncall): good. I'll do a handoff to julia for postmortem and further root cause. sam, please monitor nodes for 1 hour. Kate keep customers updated. If anything spikes, page me.

sam (eng-sre): monitoring window started. Will report if NotReady or OOM events reappear.

kate (support): customers acknowledged. Two enterprise customers requested an RCA and timeline; I'll collect notes for postmortem.

julia (eng-runtime): creating incident doc and initial timeline in INC-1029: suspected kv-cache growth + batch config change + burst traffic -> host OOM -> kubelet restart -> node NotReady -> pod evictions -> user-facing 503s. Will include mitigations and followups.

mohit (oncall): handoff complete. I'm marking on-call status -> relieved. Thanks team. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident INC-1029 updated: status -> mitigated, owner -> julia. Follow-ups assigned: runtime PR rollback review, kubelet cgroup limit audit, autoscaler policy review.

julia (eng-runtime): quick notes for followups: 1) revert kv-cache-size bump pending perf eval 2) add hard host-memory guard to autoscaler 3) add a node-level OOM monitor alert to detect early memory pressure.

sam (eng-sre): copying logs to incident ticket and attaching node dmesg + kubelet journals.

kate (support): adding customer communications to the ticket. Will coordinate with CSMs for proactive outreach.

mohit (oncall): closing the thread here. If anything flares, reopen.
